_what: Repo-tracked ingest settings. scripts/ingest-history.mjs reads this file on every run. Two things made this file necessary: the automation token cannot CREATE a workflow dispatch event (HTTP 403 on /actions/workflows/{id}/dispatches), and the daily workflow passes a fixed set of flags. Pushing a change to this file (or to .github/triggers/ingest.json) triggers the on-demand workflow, which then picks these settings up on the GitHub-hosted runner — the sandbox itself cannot open TLS to *.kalshi.com. NB: the earlier version of this note claimed a ruleset blocks workflow-file pushes; that was tested (commit c23be4d, reverted in eb1bfd2) and is FALSE — workflow files push fine, only the dispatch API is forbidden.

_schema.intraday.enabled: boolean — when true, every daily run also performs the intraday passes listed in intraday.blocks
_schema.intraday.blocks[].status: GET /markets discovery filter for block.series: open (default) | settled | all. 'settled'/'all' also ingest FINALIZED markets so their real exchange result (status=finalized, result yes/no) is stored with the bars — the only honest input for backtesting a series whose markets expire in days
_schema.intraday.blocks[].days: backfill window in days (0 = from each market's real open_time)
_schema.intraday.blocks[].max_bars: keep only the newest N bars per market (0 = unbounded); trimming is recorded in store.trims
_schema.intraday.blocks[].tickers: explicit markets. Kept short on purpose: intraday bars are ~24x as many rows as daily bars
_schema.intraday.blocks[].series: discover markets inside these series (ranked by the exchange's own lifetime volume, capped by max_markets, floored by min_volume)

blocks.name: hourly-indices
blocks._why_these: Curated by LIFETIME CONTRACT VOLUME reported by the exchange (market.volume_fp in the daily store, see data/history/_manifest.json): the ten highest-volume KXBTCY strikes (the fee-free series; 2.0M-2.7M contracts each) plus KXNASDAQ100Y-26DEC31H1600-T19000 (1.27M) and KXINXY-26DEC31H1600-B8100 (507k). 12 markets x <=336 hourly bars keeps the store near 2 MB and the browser module near 400 KB, and the universe is described by a rule rather than by preference.
blocks._why_not_all: The first intraday run inherited the daily run's --series flag and ingested all 117 open markets of the three series (40,039 bars, 22 MB, ~1.3 MB/day of growth, ~630 HTTP requests per run, mostly zero-volume strikes). scripts/prune-intraday.mjs removed them and recorded every one in data/history/intraday/60m/_prune-ledger.json with its own restore command. inherit_cli_universe is now false by default.

blocks.name: hourly-weather-cities
blocks._why_this: ROADMAP item #3 (more weather cities) as answered by the REAL series list captured by scripts/discover-universe.mjs on 2026-09-18: 54 KXHIGH* series exist and the eight ingested here are the highest by exchange-reported lifetime volume (KXHIGHLAX 166.2M, KXHIGHNY 144.6M, KXHIGHCHI 110.1M, KXHIGHMIA 98.5M, KXHIGHAUS 77.2M, KXHIGHDEN 50.8M, KXHIGHPHIL 41.5M, KXHIGHTPHX 16.8M, KXHIGHTSEA 16.5M). status=all ingests FINALIZED brackets so each carries the exchange result the replay settles on. Every one of these series has fee_multiplier 1 (data/discovered/series-fees.json), so the documented default fee model is the REAL configuration for all of them.

blocks.name: hourly-weather-settled
blocks._why_this: ROADMAP item #3 (weather markets — the most-reported retail edge in the research ledger, R06/R03/R10). KXHIGHNY is the NYC daily-high series used by Kalshi's own API quick-start (https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/quick_start_market_data). status=all also ingests FINALIZED brackets, each of which carries the exchange's REAL result — the first tracked markets in this repository that actually settle, which is what the replay needs to book real $1/$0 cash flows instead of marking to the last quote. days=0 backfills each bracket from its own open_time (a bracket lives ~1-3 days); max_backfill_days=60 bounds the lookback; the top-40-by-volume cap keeps the pass bounded (~40 markets x <=48 hourly bars).

blocks.name: minute-gold-15m-markets
blocks._why_this: ROADMAP item #4 (one-minute candles). KXGOLD15M is Kalshi's 15-minute gold series (verified to trade heavily: third-party archives list individual 15-minute contracts with 3,000-7,000 trades). A 15-minute market has ~15 one-minute bars, so max_markets=8 x ~15 bars is tiny; the 96-bar cap and the 2-day window keep a cold store from pulling a long history. 1-minute bars are the resolution the R01 panic-fade source actually traded, so this store lets that family be tested at its native granularity.

blocks.name: hourly-sports-game-lines
blocks._why_this: ROADMAP item #5: a SPORTS series was the biggest signal-ledger gap. These seven are the highest-volume game market classes the exchange reports (KXNFLGAME 6.01B, KXMLBGAME 9.80B, KXNBAGAME 11.68B, KXNHLGAME 1.57B, KXNCAAFGAME 4.78B, KXWNBAGAME 1.08B, KXUFCFIGHT 1.28B lifetime contracts). A game market lives hours, so 60-minute bars are its natural resolution, and status=all keeps the FINALIZED games whose result the exchange published — the only markets whose settlement this replay may book. NOTE the real fee config: the MLB series carry fee_multiplier 0.5 (data/discovered/series-fees.json), which the fee engine applies per series.

blocks.name: minute-crypto-15m
blocks._why_this: The three highest-volume 15-minute crypto series (KXBTC15M 18.15B, KXETH15M 972M, KXSOL15M 347M lifetime contracts) at one-minute resolution — the same treatment KXGOLD15M already gets. These are the fastest-settling markets on the exchange (15 minutes), so they produce the most independent settlement events per day for the micro flight.

blocks.name: minute-mlb-game-lines
blocks._why_this: ROADMAP Next #3 (the sports half of the point-in-time signal archive, 2026-09-20): the KXMLBGAME contracts that the official MLB game-state archive (data/mlb-signals/, statsapi.mlb.com every 20 minutes) can be joined to by ticker (fact V113). In-play repricing happens in minutes, so the hourly block (hourly-sports-game-lines) is too coarse to replay it: this block ingests the same series at period_interval=1. status=all ingests FINALIZED games with the exchange's real result; days=2 covers the games the archive observed since the previous run; max_bars=480 keeps the newest eight hours per contract (pre-game + the game itself); the top-24-by-volume cap bounds the pass (~72 requests). Contracts that finished before the 2-day window come back with 0 bars and are recorded as not replayable, never guessed.

blocks.name: hourly-macro-settled
blocks._why_this: The two macro series the roster already names but has no bars for: KXFEDDECISION (611.7M lifetime contracts, fee_multiplier 1, mutually exclusive buckets) and KXCPIYOY (36.1M, BLS settlement). Both settle on a published official number, which makes their real result an unambiguous settlement input.

blocks.name: daily-fda-approvals
blocks._why_this: The user's own source list names 'FDA Decisions Drug Analysis' as a strategy family, and the discovery run (data/discovered/series-fees.json) returned these series as REAL: KXFDAAPPROVALPSYCHEDELIC (387,164 lifetime contracts), KXFDAANNOUNCE (100,001), KXFDAAPPROVE (74,690), KXFDARETATRUTIDE (38,989), plus two dated-approval series. A 1440-minute block (periodDir(1440) == data/history/, i.e. the DAILY store the daily flight replays) gives each market a real daily price path from its own open_time, and status=all stores whatever the exchange has already finalized so the replay books the REAL result. min_volume 0 on purpose: approval markets are thin (some have 0 lifetime volume), and the strategy that reads them must abstain on a market with no tradable path rather than be fed a filtered sample.

blocks.name: daily-ceo-exits
blocks._why_this: The user's source list names 'CEO' (MasterSite) as a strategy family and 'insider trades' alongside it. These are the highest-volume real CEO-exit series returned by the discovery run: KXAAPLCEOCHANGE (587,863), KXTESLACEOCHANGE (512,304), KXOPENAICEOCHANGE (223,770), KXJPMCEOCHANGE (119,462), KXGOOGLECEOCHANGE (88,680), KXBOEINGCEOCHANGE (151,313). Same storage reasoning as daily-fda-approvals: 1440-minute bars land in the daily store, status=all captures the exchange's own result for any market it has finalized.
